name: GXO Logistics
desc: Contract logistics operator running warehouses and fulfilment for retail, e-commerce, consumer goods and healthcare customers.
markets: Customers across the US, UK and Europe; acquired UK group Wincanton in 2024 to expand British operations.
rationale: Warehouse automation showcase and B2B hospitality for retail and consumer-goods clients; limited consumer brand, though logistics rivals DHL and CEVA already partner with F1.
changed: Spun off from XPO in 2021

name: Impala Terminals
desc: Operates port terminals, warehousing, river transport and logistics services for metals, minerals and agricultural commodities.
markets: Terminals and logistics serving commodity traders and miners in Latin America and Africa; part of the Trafigura group.
rationale: B2B commodities infrastructure with no consumer brand; hospitality value for mining and trading clients is real but narrow.

name: J.B. Hunt Transport
desc: Provides intermodal container, dedicated contract, truckload and final-mile delivery transportation services across North America.
markets: Customers in the US, Canada and Mexico; intermodal services run with railroad partners.
rationale: Large B2B shipper base suits hospitality, but business is North America focused with little consumer brand to build globally.

name: Phillips 66
desc: Refines petroleum, operates midstream pipelines and chemicals, and sells fuels and lubricants including the Phillips 66 and Kendall brands.
markets: Refineries and marketing in the US and Europe; sells fuels and lubricants to retail and commercial customers.
rationale: Lubricants and fuel brands fit motorsport marketing; established F1 energy and lubricant partners are direct competitors for category presence.
changed: Spun out of ConocoPhillips in 2012

name: Wabtec
desc: Makes locomotives, braking and signalling systems and other equipment and services for freight and transit rail customers worldwide.
markets: Sells to railways in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and elsewhere; bought GE Transportation in 2019.
rationale: Engineering and technology showcase with B2B hospitality for railway customers; low consumer awareness limits brand-building value.
changed: Merged with GE Transportation in 2019

name: Scan Global Logistics
desc: Provides air, sea and road freight forwarding, contract logistics and project cargo services through offices in dozens of countries.
markets: Importers and exporters served via a worldwide office network built through many acquisitions; privately held with private equity backing.
rationale: B2B freight forwarder that could use F1 hospitality for customers and its logistics ties to the sport; logistics rivals already partner.

name: Archion
desc: Holding company combining truck makers Hino Motors and Mitsubishi Fuso Truck and Bus under shared Toyota and Daimler Truck ownership.
markets: Japanese and Asian truck markets, with Hino and Fuso selling trucks and buses in other regions as well.
rationale: Commercial-vehicle maker with two major motorsport-linked shareholders; B2B truck brand with limited consumer reach, but technology and hospitality interest.
changed: Formed to combine Hino and Mitsubishi Fuso
f1: Co-owner Daimler Truck is an F1 partner (Mercedes-Benz Trucks); co-owner Toyota owns Toyota Gazoo Racing, linked to Haas

name: China State Railway Group Co.
desc: Operates China's national rail network, including passenger services, the high-speed network and freight transport.
markets: Passenger and freight customers across China; foreign operations are limited to cooperation projects.
rationale: State railway monopoly with no commercial need for brand sponsorship; very limited F1 fit.
changed: Formerly China Railway Corporation; renamed in 2019

name: European Locomotive Leasing
desc: Leases modern electric locomotives, notably Siemens Vectron models, to rail freight and passenger operators and offers related services.
markets: Rail operators across Europe lease its locomotives; business is equipment financing and servicing.
rationale: B2B equipment lessor with no consumer exposure; weak F1 fit beyond occasional hospitality.

name: Knight-Swift Transportation
desc: Largest US full truckload carrier, also running less-than-truckload, logistics and intermodal services under Knight, Swift and other brands.
markets: Shippers in the US and Mexico; formed by the 2017 merger of Knight and Swift Transportation.
rationale: Domestic trucking brand with a large customer base, but North America focus makes F1 a stretch.
changed: Knight and Swift merged in 2017

name: RXO
desc: Asset-light freight platform offering truck brokerage, last-mile delivery of heavy goods and managed transportation services.
markets: Shippers and carriers in the US; spun off from XPO in 2022.
rationale: Technology-led freight marketplace could use B2B hospitality, but its customers are North American and the brand is little known.
changed: Spun off from XPO in 2022

name: V2X
desc: Provides base operations, logistics, aircraft maintenance, training and mission support services to the US military and allied governments.
markets: US Department of Defense and allied government customers at bases worldwide; formed in 2022 from Vectrus and Vertex Aerospace.
rationale: Government contractor with no consumer brand; sponsorship value is mostly recruitment and hospitality, which is limited.
changed: Vectrus and Vertex Aerospace combined in 2022

name: CRRC
desc: World's largest rail equipment maker, producing high-speed trains, locomotives, metro cars, freight wagons and components.
markets: Exports trains and metro cars to Asia, Europe, the Americas, Africa and Oceania; large home market in China.
rationale: Global rail brand under state control with export ambitions; engineering showcase possible but little consumer marketing tradition.
changed: Formed by merger of CNR and CSR in 2015

name: Mini Mall Storage
desc: Offers self-storage facilities and solutions in Alberta, according to the Crunchbase description.
markets: Appears to serve customers around Calgary, Alberta; no international activity known.
rationale: Local storage operator with no evident international growth plans; very weak F1 fit.

name: Tristar Transport
desc: Transports and stores bulk liquids such as fuel, chemicals and lubricants by road, sea and terminals.
markets: Part of Tristar Group, serving energy and chemicals customers in the Middle East, Africa and Asia.
rationale: Fuel and lubricants logistics ties naturally to F1's energy partners, but it is a B2B brand with modest marketing needs.

name: Warehouses De Pauw
desc: Belgian listed property trust that develops, owns and leases logistics warehouses and distribution centres in several European countries.
markets: Tenants in Belgium, the Netherlands, France, Germany, Luxembourg and Romania.
rationale: Landlord with few consumer touchpoints; F1 hospitality could serve tenants, but marketing value is small.

name: Werner Enterprises
desc: Truckload carrier and logistics provider running dry van, flatbed, temperature-controlled and dedicated fleets plus brokerage and final-mile services.
markets: Customers in the US, Canada and Mexico, including cross-border Mexico services.
rationale: Domestic trucking brand with limited international ambition; F1 is a weak fit.

name: Full Truck Alliance
desc: Runs China's largest digital freight platform matching shippers with truck drivers, plus financing, fuel and insurance services.
markets: Shippers and truck drivers in mainland China; no significant overseas operations known.
rationale: Technology platform with a large China user base; F1 offers little reach for a domestic freight app.
changed: Created by merger of Yunmanman and Huochebang in 2017

name: Via
desc: Provides ride-sharing and public-transit software to cities, transit agencies and school districts.
markets: Municipal and transit customers in the US and Europe, plus other regions.
rationale: Mobility technology firm that could use F1 as a technology showcase for city and transit buyers; consumer brand is small.
changed: Went public via IPO in 2025

name: Quick Quack Car Wash
desc: Operates express drive-through car wash locations selling single washes and monthly membership subscriptions.
markets: Customers are local drivers across the western and southern US; no international operations.
rationale: Regional US consumer brand with no international footprint; F1 offers poor return.

name: Brambles
desc: Supplies and manages reusable pallets and crates, mainly under the CHEP brand, to manufacturers and retailers.
markets: Operates in around 60 countries across the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Africa.
rationale: Global supply-chain brand with blue-chip customers; B2B hospitality and sustainability story suit F1, though consumer awareness is low.

name: Flexport
desc: Digital freight forwarder moving goods by air, ocean and truck for importers and exporters on a technology platform.
markets: Shippers worldwide, with offices across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Technology-led forwarder that could showcase its platform and entertain shippers; F1 sits well with its supply-chain visibility pitch.

name: UTM Offshore
desc: Provides marine logistics and offshore vessel services for oil and gas companies, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Appears to serve oil and gas operators in Nigeria; international activity not confirmed.
rationale: B2B offshore services firm with no consumer brand and limited public information; weak F1 fit.

name: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India
desc: Builds and operates freight-only railway corridors in India, on the Eastern and Western routes.
markets: Indian freight rail customers; wholly owned by the Government of India.
rationale: Government-owned infrastructure body with no commercial brand to promote; F1 fit is very weak.

name: Emergent Cold Latin America
desc: Operates temperature-controlled warehousing and cold chain logistics in Latin America, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Cold storage facilities serving food customers in Latin America; head office is in Dallas.
rationale: B2B cold-chain operator with little consumer brand; hospitality value for food clients exists but F1 fit is weak.

name: FNM
desc: Italian rail and transport group running Lombardy regional rail services, including Trenord and Malpensa Express, plus rail infrastructure.
markets: Passengers and rail concessions in Lombardy, northern Italy; majority held by the Lombardy region.
rationale: Regional public-transport brand with a Lombardy audience, and Monza is nearby, but marketing value to F1 is small.

name: Talgo
desc: Manufactures intercity, regional and high-speed passenger trains, known for lightweight articulated rolling stock and variable-gauge axles.
markets: Sells trains to national railways and operators in Spain, Europe, Central Asia and the Middle East.
rationale: Rolling stock maker with Spanish and Middle East customers; B2B engineering showcase possible, but limited marketing budget and consumer reach.

name: Industrial Logistics Properties Trust
desc: Real estate investment trust owning and leasing industrial and logistics properties, mainly Oahu land in Hawaii and US mainland warehouses.
markets: Tenants are in the US, mostly in Hawaii and mainland warehouse markets.
rationale: Property trust with no consumer brand or international business; F1 fit is minimal.

name: GLP
desc: Investment manager and operator of logistics real estate, data centres and renewable energy assets worldwide.
markets: Warehouses and funds across Asia, Europe, the Americas; formerly Global Logistic Properties.
rationale: Institutional property manager that could use F1 to entertain investors and tenants, but consumer awareness is minimal.
changed: Taken private in 2018; formerly Global Logistic Properties

name: Logisteed
desc: Third-party logistics provider offering contract logistics, freight forwarding, warehousing and supply chain services to manufacturers and retailers.
markets: Customers in Japan, Asia, Europe and the Americas; formerly Hitachi Transport System.
rationale: Japanese logistics firm with global ambitions and B2B clients in automotive and electronics; strong in hospitality, little consumer branding.
changed: Formerly Hitachi Transport System; taken private by KKR in 2023

name: FlashEX
desc: Intracity express delivery service using a crowdsourced courier network to deliver parcels, documents and food on demand.
markets: Consumers and businesses in Chinese cities; also known as Shansong.
rationale: Domestic on-demand courier with no overseas ambitions and a mismatch with F1's audience; very weak fit.

name: UniUni
desc: Last-mile parcel delivery for e-commerce sellers and cross-border merchants in Canada and the United States.
markets: Online retailers and merchants shipping within Canada and the US.
rationale: Growing e-commerce courier that could use F1 hospitality, but it has little consumer awareness and is mainly North American.

name: Citibox
desc: Operates smart parcel lockers in residential buildings and public places so e-commerce parcels can be collected at any time.
markets: Property owners and carriers in Spain; wider European operations not confirmed here.
rationale: Locker network with limited brand and mostly Spanish footprint; F1 is a weak fit despite Spanish Grand Prix presence.

name: Country Delight
desc: Direct-to-consumer subscription service delivering milk, dairy, fruit, vegetables and staples to urban households through its app.
markets: Urban Indian households; sources from farmers and runs its own delivery network.
rationale: Indian consumer brand with growing awareness, but domestic focus; F1 has limited reach for its customer base.

name: Shadowfax Technologies
desc: Last-mile delivery technology company serving e-commerce, food and quick-commerce clients through a network of gig-economy riders.
markets: Clients such as Flipkart, Zomato, Swiggy and Meesho delivering across Indian cities.
rationale: B2B delivery platform with clients in India only; F1 appeal is small.

name: Catena
desc: Swedish property company that develops, owns and manages logistics properties let to retailers, distributors and third-party logistics operators.
markets: Logistics properties let to retailers and distributors in Sweden, Denmark and Finland; no expansion beyond the Nordics known.
rationale: Nordic landlord with no consumer brand, so F1 hospitality or sponsorship would add very little value.

name: TORM
desc: Owns and operates product tankers carrying refined oil products such as diesel, petrol and jet fuel worldwide.
markets: Charters tankers to oil majors and traders on global trade routes.
rationale: B2B tanker owner serving oil majors that sponsor F1; hospitality possible, but no consumer brand.

name: Getlink
desc: Operates the Channel Tunnel, including the Eurotunnel Le Shuttle car and truck service, plus Europorte rail freight and ElecLink.
markets: Passengers and freight between the UK and France; ElecLink power interconnector and Europorte freight in France.
rationale: UK-France consumer travel brand with a corporate base; F1 offers a European audience, though business is concession-based.

name: HEA Energy
desc: Offshore marine logistics company supporting the energy industry with vessels and offshore support services, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Appears to serve oil and gas operators in the Gulf; no other activity confirmed.
rationale: B2B offshore services provider with little public information; F1 fit is weak.

name: Pensana
desc: Develops the Longonjo rare earths project in Angola and a rare earth processing hub in Hull, England.
markets: Pre-revenue; planned supply of magnet rare earth oxides from Angola and the UK to magnet makers.
rationale: Pre-revenue developer without a consumer brand; F1 is more a financing story than a marketing one.

name: Rotterdam World Gateway
desc: Automated deep-sea container terminal at Maasvlakte 2 in the Port of Rotterdam, run as a four-company joint venture.
markets: Handles containers for shipping lines at one Rotterdam terminal; partners are DP World, Hutchison Ports, MOL and HMM.
rationale: Single-terminal joint venture with shipping-line customers; no consumer brand, so F1 sponsorship would be hard to justify.
f1: Joint-venture shareholder DP World is an F1 partner; DP World is not the parent

name: SAL
desc: Saudi air cargo and logistics company offering air freight, ground handling, warehousing and logistics services at Saudi airports.
markets: Subsidiary of Saudia Group; air freight to Europe, Asia and North America plus Saudi ground handling.
rationale: Saudi state-linked cargo brand where F1's Saudi Arabian Grand Prix and Aramco ties give regional relevance; B2B with limited consumer reach.

name: Cainiao Logistics
desc: Logistics arm of Alibaba Group running a smart logistics network linking warehouses, couriers and cross-border delivery for e-commerce.
markets: Cross-border and domestic delivery for Alibaba merchants, with hubs in Asia, Europe and elsewhere.
rationale: Alibaba-backed logistics brand with global ambitions and technology story; F1 could support cross-border brand building.

name: Deliveroo
desc: Online food delivery platform connecting restaurants, grocers and riders with customers in the UK, Ireland, France, Italy and Gulf.
markets: Operates in the UK, Ireland, France, Italy, Belgium, the UAE, Kuwait and Qatar.
rationale: Consumer app with young urban audience and Gulf presence near F1 races; now owned by DoorDash, so budget decisions sit with the parent.
changed: Acquired by DoorDash in 2025

name: Just Eat Takeaway.com
desc: Online food delivery marketplace formed by merging Just Eat and Takeaway.com, operating across the UK, Germany, Netherlands and other markets.
markets: Consumer marketplace across the UK, Germany, the Netherlands, Canada and other European countries.
rationale: Established consumer brand in several F1 markets; now under Prosus ownership, so sponsorship depends on the new owner's priorities.
changed: Merged in 2020; acquired by Prosus in 2025

name: Lalamove
desc: On-demand logistics platform connecting customers and small businesses with van, truck and motorbike drivers for same-day delivery and moving.
markets: Operates in Asia and Latin America, including Hong Kong, mainland China, Southeast Asia, India and Brazil.
rationale: Consumer and SME app with multi-region ambitions, giving a marketing case in Asian F1 markets; sponsorship would be brand-awareness driven.

name: Picard Surgelés
desc: French frozen food retailer selling own-brand frozen meals, vegetables, desserts and other products through its own shops and online.
markets: Shops mainly in France, with stores in other European countries.
rationale: Strong French consumer brand with food-led appeal, but limited reach beyond Europe; F1 value would rest on French fans and hospitality.

name: Gorillas
desc: Quick-commerce grocery delivery start-up that promised delivery within minutes from dark stores in several European countries.
markets: Operated in Germany, the UK, France, the Netherlands and the US before a retreat; sold to Getir in 2022.
rationale: Brand no longer operates independently after being sold and wound down, so there is no sponsorship case at all.
changed: Acquired by Getir in 2022; brand later wound down

name: Ouyeel Industrial Products
desc: B2B platform for industrial products and steel supply chain services, offering e-commerce, logistics and related services.
markets: Industrial buyers and sellers in China; part of China Baowu steel group's Ouyeel ecosystem.
rationale: State-linked B2B platform with no consumer brand and domestic focus; F1 has little relevance.

name: Xpressbees
desc: E-commerce logistics company providing parcel delivery, cross-border, warehousing and freight services across most Indian pin codes.
markets: Online retailers and sellers shipping parcels within India; no overseas operations or expansion plans known.
rationale: Indian B2B courier with little consumer brand and domestic focus; F1 is a weak fit.

name: Fetch
desc: Last-mile logistics and resident service platform for apartment buildings, handling package deliveries, parcel lockers and resident services.
markets: Property owners and tenants in the US; separate from the Fetch rewards app.
rationale: Property-services start-up with no consumer brand and US-only footprint; F1 offers little return.

name: inDrive
desc: Ride-hailing and urban services app where riders negotiate fares directly with drivers, also offering delivery and other services.
markets: Operates in dozens of countries across Latin America, Asia, Africa, Europe and the Middle East.
rationale: Consumer app with broad emerging-market reach and heavy brand spend; F1's global audience could support awareness campaigns.
changed: Originally founded in Russia as Indriver

name: ClearWater Express Wash
desc: Operates and develops express drive-through car wash sites, selling single washes and monthly memberships.
markets: Local drivers in its regional US markets; no international operations or expansion plans known.
rationale: Regional US car wash chain with no international ambitions; F1 is a poor fit.

name: CookUnity
desc: Meal subscription service delivering chef-prepared ready-to-heat meals from its own kitchens across the United States.
markets: Consumers across the US; no international operations known.
rationale: US-only direct-to-consumer brand; F1 has limited audience overlap and a heavy cost.

name: Interfor
desc: Large Canadian softwood lumber producer operating sawmills and selling lumber for housing and construction.
markets: Sawmills in Canada and the US; lumber sold to North American and Asian customers.
rationale: Commodity lumber producer without a consumer brand or marketing culture; Formula 1 is a weak fit commercially.

name: Porter
desc: Intracity logistics platform connecting customers with trucks, two-wheelers and tempos for goods transport, plus packers and movers.
markets: Consumers and small businesses in Indian cities; no overseas operations or expansion plans known.
rationale: Indian logistics app with domestic focus; F1 offers limited reach for its customers.

name: Zapp
desc: Rapid convenience-store delivery start-up delivering groceries in minutes from dark stores, mainly in London.
markets: Consumers mainly in central London and the UK; has since scaled back.
rationale: Small London delivery brand that has scaled back; F1 spend would be hard to justify.

name: Ninja
desc: Quick-commerce app delivering groceries and household items in minutes from local dark stores in Saudi cities.
markets: Urban consumers in Saudi Arabia; no international expansion confirmed.
rationale: Fast-growing Saudi consumer app with heavy marketing; the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix gives local reach, but expansion beyond the kingdom is unconfirmed.

name: Danaos
desc: Owns containerships and charters them to liner companies on long-term contracts.
markets: Charters vessels to major container lines serving worldwide trade routes.
rationale: B2B ship owner with no consumer brand; hospitality value is thin and F1 is a poor fit.

name: Forward Air
desc: Provides expedited ground freight, airport-to-airport and last-mile delivery services to airlines, freight forwarders and shippers.
markets: Customers in the US; operates a national airport-to-airport network.
rationale: US-focused B2B freight carrier with little consumer awareness; F1 is a weak fit.

name: Americold
desc: Provides temperature-controlled warehousing and logistics services to food producers and retailers; the Crunchbase location is in South Australia.
markets: Cold storage customers in Australia; the related Americold Realty is a US-listed group with global warehouses.
rationale: B2B cold-storage business without consumer brand; the match between this Australian listing and the US parent is unconfirmed.

name: American Industrial Transport
desc: Provides railcar leasing and rail transportation services to freight shipping customers in the United States.
markets: Freight shippers in the US; ownership and fleet details are not confirmed.
rationale: B2B railcar business with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship makes little commercial sense.

name: Warrior Met Coal
desc: Produces and exports metallurgical coal from Alabama mines for steelmakers.
markets: Customers are steelmakers in Europe, Asia and South America; mines in Alabama.
rationale: Commodity coal miner with no consumer brand; sustainability concerns make F1 an unlikely partner.

name: Global Ship Lease
desc: Owns mid-size and smaller containerships and charters them to liner companies such as CMA CGM, Maersk and ZIM.
markets: Long-term charters to liner customers on global container trade lanes.
rationale: B2B ship lessor with no consumer brand; sponsoring F1 would add little commercial value.

name: Okeanis Eco Tankers
desc: Owns modern crude oil tankers (VLCCs and Suezmaxes) and charters them to oil majors and traders.
markets: Spot-market charters to oil majors and traders on worldwide routes.
rationale: B2B tanker owner with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit despite oil-major customers.

name: Star Bulk Carriers
desc: Owns and operates dry bulk vessels carrying iron ore, coal, grain and other cargoes around the world.
markets: Fleet of about 150 Capesize, Kamsarmax and other vessels on global commodity routes.
rationale: B2B bulk shipper with no consumer exposure; F1 sponsorship offers little value.

name: Blue Raven Solutions
desc: Supply chain and fleet management company, according to Crunchbase; scale and customers are not confirmed.
markets: Appears to serve US customers; customers and any international activity are not confirmed.
rationale: Little public information and no known consumer brand; F1 case cannot be supported.

name: Flock Freight
desc: Freight technology company offering shared truckload shipping that pools several shippers' freight in one truck.
markets: Shippers in the US; no international operations known.
rationale: Technology-led shipper with sustainability pitch, but US-only business gives F1 little reach.

name: Volare Shipping
desc: Global shipping business based in Singapore, according to Crunchbase; fleet, customers and ownership are not confirmed.
markets: Described as a global shipping business; no verified fleet or customer details are available.
rationale: Little public information and no consumer brand; F1 case cannot be supported.

name: Radiant Logistics
desc: Non-asset-based third-party logistics provider offering truck brokerage, air and ocean freight, customs brokerage and warehousing.
markets: Shippers in North America plus air and ocean freight services to other regions.
rationale: B2B freight forwarder with little consumer awareness; hospitality could serve shippers, but F1 fit is weak.

name: Shanghai International Port Group
desc: Operates Shanghai's container terminals, including Yangshan Deep Water Port, with stakes in other Chinese and overseas terminals.
markets: Shipping-line customers at Shanghai ports, plus overseas terminal investments such as Haifa.
rationale: State-controlled port operator with no consumer brand; relevance to F1 is limited to Chinese Grand Prix links.

name: STG Logistics
desc: Asset-light provider of drayage, intermodal, trucking and warehousing services, formed as a private equity backed roll-up.
markets: Shippers in the US; no international activity known.
rationale: B2B logistics roll-up with no consumer brand and financial restructuring history; F1 fit is very weak.
changed: Filed Chapter 11 in 2023 and restructured

name: Unitop
desc: Chinese logistics and supply chain company, according to Crunchbase; customers and scale are not confirmed.
markets: Appears to serve customers in China; international activity not confirmed.
rationale: Little public information and no consumer brand; F1 fit cannot be established.

name: Glovo
desc: On-demand delivery app for meals, groceries and parcels in about 25 countries across Southern and Eastern Europe, Africa, Central Asia.
markets: Consumers in Spain, Italy, Portugal, Eastern Europe, Africa and Central Asia; owned by Delivery Hero.
rationale: Consumer app with young audience and Spanish Grand Prix link; owned by Delivery Hero, so group decisions drive budgets.
changed: Acquired by Delivery Hero (majority control from 2022)

name: Kazakhstan Temir Zholy
desc: Kazakhstan's national railway company operating freight and passenger rail, ports, the Aktau terminal and the Trans-Caspian route.
markets: Rail freight across Kazakhstan and Central Asia, with Trans-Caspian and China-Europe corridor traffic.
rationale: State rail operator with transit-corridor ambitions; consumer marketing is minimal and F1 is a distant fit.

name: STO Express
desc: Chinese express parcel delivery company handling large volumes of parcels through a franchise network of outlets.
markets: Domestic Chinese e-commerce parcels; one of China's large courier firms.
rationale: Domestic courier with limited overseas business and little consumer marketing; F1 sponsorship is a weak fit.

name: Hive Box
desc: Operates smart self-service parcel lockers across China, installed in residential communities and campuses.
markets: Parcel pick-up lockers in Chinese communities; no international operations known.
rationale: Domestic locker network with little brand reach abroad; F1 is a weak fit.

name: Shanghai ANE Logistics
desc: Less-than-truckload and express logistics company running a transport line and delivery point network for cargo shipping in China.
markets: Cargo customers in China; no international activity known.
rationale: B2B freight network with little brand reach outside China; F1 fit is weak.

name: Uber Freight
desc: Digital freight marketplace and brokerage connecting shippers with truck drivers and carriers, plus transportation management services.
markets: Shippers and carriers mainly in the US, with operations in Canada, Mexico and Europe; Uber's logistics arm.
rationale: Technology-led freight brand within Uber with an enterprise shipper base; F1 offers tech showcase and hospitality, though budget sits with Uber.

name: Ecom Express
desc: E-commerce logistics company delivering parcels for online retailers such as Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra across most Indian pin codes.
markets: Online retailers shipping parcels within India; no overseas operations or expansion plans known.
rationale: Indian B2B courier with little consumer brand; F1 has a weak fit.

name: Blue Apron
desc: Meal-kit company that delivered subscription boxes of pre-portioned ingredients and recipes to US households.
markets: Households in the US only; no international operations or expansion plans known for the brand.
rationale: Brand was taken over and has little independent marketing presence; F1 is not a realistic fit.
changed: Delisted and acquired by Wonder Group in 2023

name: Paack
desc: Technology-driven last-mile delivery company handling e-commerce parcels for retailers using drivers and parcel lockers.
markets: Retailers in Spain, Portugal, France and Italy; parcel lockers and drivers support last-mile delivery.
rationale: B2B delivery brand with Spanish base and little consumer awareness; F1 hospitality offers modest value.

name: Zippy Shell
desc: Franchise system delivering portable storage containers to customers for local or long-distance moves or storage.
markets: Franchise customers moving or storing goods in the US only; no international operations or expansion plans known.
rationale: Small US franchise brand with no international ambitions; F1 fit is minimal.

name: HungryPanda
desc: Food delivery platform serving Chinese and Asian restaurants for overseas Chinese communities and international students, now also groceries.
markets: Operates in the UK, US, Europe, Australia, Japan and other countries via its app.
rationale: Consumer brand with strong diaspora recognition across several F1 markets; sponsorship could target Asian communities and students.

name: Spyglass Pharma
desc: Specialty ophthalmic pharmaceutical company developing a drug-delivery implant releasing glaucoma medication over several months.
markets: Pre-revenue; development based in the US with no commercial sales yet.
rationale: Pre-revenue ophthalmic drug developer with no consumer brand to market; F1 partnership is a weak fit.

name: Everli
desc: Online grocery marketplace where personal shoppers pick and deliver goods from local supermarkets such as Carrefour.
markets: Consumers in Italy and other European countries; formerly Supermercato24.
rationale: Italian consumer app with Monza Grand Prix relevance; limited marketing budget and mainly southern European audience.
changed: Renamed from Supermercato24 to Everli

name: VTG
desc: Owns and leases rail wagons, tank containers and offers rail logistics services across Europe.
markets: Fleet of about 90,000 railcars leased to chemicals, energy and other industrial customers mainly in Europe.
rationale: B2B wagon lessor with little consumer brand; F1 hospitality could serve industrial customers but fit is weak.

name: CPV Generation Holdings
desc: Holding entity for natural gas power plants owned by Competitive Power Ventures, a US power developer and operator.
markets: Sells electricity and capacity into US wholesale power markets; no international activity known.
rationale: Power-generation holding vehicle with no consumer brand to market; an F1 partnership makes minimal commercial sense.

name: Navios Maritime Partners
desc: Publicly traded partnership owning and chartering dry bulk vessels, containerships and tankers to commodity traders, container lines and oil companies.
markets: Charters about 150 vessels to commodity traders, container lines and oil companies worldwide.
rationale: B2B ship owner with no consumer profile; F1 sponsorship would add little commercial value.

name: Cabify
desc: Ride-hailing and mobility company offering app-based taxi and private car services, mainly in Spain and Latin America.
markets: Consumers in Spain and Latin America, including Mexico, Chile and Colombia.
rationale: Consumer mobility brand with Spanish and Latin American reach that overlap F1 races in Spain and Mexico.

name: Ceske Drahy
desc: Czech Republic's national railway passenger operator running domestic and international passenger trains.
markets: Passengers in the Czech Republic with international services to neighbouring European countries.
rationale: State-owned rail operator with little marketing need beyond Czech passengers; F1 is a weak fit.

name: COSCO SHIPPING
desc: Chinese state-owned shipping and logistics group operating container shipping, terminals, bulk and tanker fleets and logistics services.
markets: Container lines, ports and logistics worldwide; formed by the 2016 merger of COSCO and China Shipping.
rationale: Global shipping brand in China-Europe trade; B2B hospitality possible, but state ownership and little consumer marketing limit the fit.
changed: Formed by merger of COSCO and China Shipping in 2016

name: Galaxy Container Solutions
desc: Logistics company offering commercial shipping and container logistics services, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Appears to operate from Boston; customers and scale are not confirmed.
rationale: Little public information and no known consumer brand; F1 case cannot be supported.

name: Kuehne + Nagel
desc: Provides sea, air, road and contract logistics services to customers in more than 100 countries.
markets: Freight forwarding and logistics across Europe, the Americas, Asia-Pacific and Africa.
rationale: Global logistics brand with large corporate customer base; F1 hospitality and supply-chain showcase fit, and rivals DHL and CEVA already partner.

name: Rand Logistics
desc: Former bulk shipping company that ran dry bulk and tanker vessels on the Great Lakes through Lower Lakes Towing.
markets: Carried grain, salt, coal and stone between the US and Canada.
rationale: Company went bankrupt and no longer operates as an independent business, so there is no sponsorship case at all.
changed: Filed for bankruptcy in 2018 and its assets were sold

name: VLI
desc: Brazilian logistics operator integrating rail, ports and terminals to move agricultural and industrial cargo such as grain and fertiliser.
markets: Cargo customers in Brazil's agricultural and mining regions; owned by Brazilian and international investors.
rationale: B2B logistics operator with no consumer brand; Brazilian Grand Prix gives local hospitality value but little else.

name: Ocean Network Express
desc: Container shipping line formed by combining the container businesses of Japan's NYK, MOL and K Line.
markets: Container services on trade lanes worldwide; formed in 2017 by Japanese shipping groups.
rationale: Global container line with large corporate customers; B2B hospitality fit is real, but consumer awareness is low.
changed: Formed in 2017 from NYK, MOL and K Line container businesses

name: NextNRG
desc: Energy technology company offering mobile fuel delivery, wireless EV charging, microgrids and AI-managed energy infrastructure.
markets: Fuel delivery customers in US states; no international operations known.
rationale: Small US-listed energy technology firm with limited marketing budget; F1 is a stretch.
changed: Formerly EzFill; renamed NextNRG

name: P N Gadgil Jewellers
desc: Indian jewellery retailer founded in 1832 selling gold, silver, diamond and platinum jewellery through stores.
markets: Customers in India through a network of stores, mainly in Maharashtra.
rationale: Heritage Indian jewellery brand with domestic customers; F1 spend is hard to justify.

name: Sihamba Sonke Mobility
desc: Operates and modernises mobility services in fleet management and logistics, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Appears to operate in South Africa; customers and ownership are not confirmed.
rationale: Little public information and no known consumer brand; F1 case cannot be supported.

name: Rumo
desc: Brazilian railway and logistics operator hauling agricultural commodities such as soy, corn and sugar to the port of Santos.
markets: Rail concession customers in Brazil's grain and sugar regions.
rationale: B2B rail concession with no consumer brand; Brazilian Grand Prix offers limited local hospitality.

name: Cimko
desc: Turkish cement and construction materials producer offering cement, ready-mix concrete and waste recovery, part of the Sanko group.
markets: Customers in Turkey for cement and ready-mix concrete; export activity and expansion plans are not confirmed.
rationale: Cement maker with domestic focus and little consumer marketing; F1 fit is weak.

name: Global Feeder Shipping
desc: Container feeder shipping line running short-sea services connecting Gulf, Indian subcontinent and Red Sea ports with transhipment hubs.
markets: Short-sea container services in the Gulf, Indian subcontinent and Red Sea region.
rationale: B2B feeder line with no consumer brand; Gulf races offer hospitality, but marketing value is small.

name: Landstar System
desc: Asset-light transportation and logistics company using thousands of independent owner-operators and agents to move freight.
markets: Shippers in the US, Canada and Mexico through independent agents; no wider international expansion known.
rationale: Large North American freight brand with little consumer awareness; F1 is a weak fit.

name: Switzer-Carty Transportation
desc: Canadian passenger transportation company offering scheduled and charter bus services, including school buses and motorcoaches.
markets: School boards, groups and commuters in Ontario only; no international operations or expansion plans known.
rationale: Local Ontario bus operator with no international footprint; F1 is a very poor fit.

name: CargoX
desc: Blockchain-based platform for electronic bills of lading and trade documents used by shipping lines, shippers and banks.
markets: Trade-document platform for shipping lines, shippers and banks; originally Slovenian with Crunchbase listing Abu Dhabi.
rationale: Niche B2B trade technology with little consumer awareness; hospitality to shipping clients is the only plausible fit.

name: Delin Property
desc: Logistics real estate investment and development platform investing in warehouses and distribution space in the UK and Europe.
markets: Tenants are logistics and e-commerce companies in the UK and Europe.
rationale: B2B landlord with no consumer profile; F1 sponsorship adds little for its tenants.

name: KNOT Offshore Partners
desc: Owns and operates shuttle tankers carrying crude oil from offshore fields to onshore terminals under long-term charters.
markets: Charters to oil majors such as Equinor, Shell and Petrobras in the North Sea and Brazil.
rationale: B2B tanker owner with no consumer profile; F1 sponsorship has little commercial use.

name: Touax
desc: Leases and sells transport equipment such as shipping containers, modular buildings, river barges and railcars.
markets: Customers in Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas.
rationale: B2B equipment lessor with no consumer brand or marketing culture; an F1 partnership is a weak fit.

name: Norfolk Southern Corporation
desc: Operates one of the largest US freight railroads, serving most major eastern ports and markets across 22 states.
markets: Rail freight customers in the eastern US; about 19,000 route miles.
rationale: US freight railroad with no consumer brand and a pending merger; F1 hospitality would be hard to justify.
changed: Union Pacific announced a deal to acquire it in 2025

name: Flash Express
desc: Thai parcel and express delivery network delivering e-commerce parcels to consumers and small businesses through branches and vans.
markets: Operations in Thailand, Malaysia, Laos and the Philippines; founded in 2018.
rationale: Fast-growing Thai delivery brand with Southeast Asian reach and Thai Grand Prix interest; F1 spend would need strong marketing returns.

name: Lobito Atlantic Railway
desc: Operates the Lobito Corridor rail line from the Angolan port of Lobito east to the Democratic Republic of Congo border.
markets: Holds a 30-year concession in Angola, linking Congo and Zambia mines to the sea.
rationale: Mining-logistics rail concession with no consumer brand; F1 is not a realistic fit.

name: Licious
desc: Direct-to-consumer brand selling fresh chicken, mutton, fish and ready-to-cook products through an app and delivery network.
markets: Consumers in Indian cities through its app and delivery network; no overseas operations or expansion plans known.
rationale: Indian consumer food brand with domestic focus; F1 offers limited audience overlap, so it is a weak fit.

name: Halan
desc: Egyptian ride-hailing and lifestyle app offering motorbike and tuk-tuk rides, delivery services and consumer financing.
markets: Consumers in Egyptian cities; no international operations known.
rationale: Egyptian consumer app with no international presence and a local customer base; F1 has little relevance.

name: Nana
desc: Saudi quick-commerce platform delivering groceries, household items and pharmacy products from partner stores and dark stores.
markets: Consumers in Saudi Arabia only; no international expansion confirmed.
rationale: Leading Saudi grocery app that could use the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix for brand awareness; expansion beyond the kingdom is unconfirmed.

name: Maison Solutions
desc: Operates Asian-American and Hispanic supermarkets in Southern California, including Good Fortune Supermarket.
markets: Stores in Southern California; no international operations known.
rationale: Small regional grocery chain with no international ambitions; F1 is a poor fit.

name: Ryde Group
desc: Carpooling and ride-hailing app connecting riders with private-car and taxi drivers, plus a delivery and advertising business.
markets: Riders and drivers in Singapore only; no confirmed overseas operations or expansion plans.
rationale: Small Singapore app that could use Singapore Grand Prix exposure, but its size limits F1 spend.

name: Stef
desc: Specialist in temperature-controlled logistics and transport, running refrigerated warehouses and trucks for fresh and frozen food.
markets: Retailers and food producers in France and other European countries.
rationale: B2B cold-chain brand with European focus; F1 hospitality might serve food clients, but marketing value is small.

name: JD Property
desc: Infrastructure asset manager of JD.com's logistics business, owning and managing logistics parks and warehouses used by JD Logistics.
markets: Customers are e-commerce and supply chain operators in China; part of JD.com.
rationale: B2B property arm of a consumer internet group with low independent brand; F1 fit is weak.

name: Convoy
desc: Digital freight network that matched truckload shipments with trucking carriers before shutting down in 2023.
markets: US shippers and carriers; ceased operations in 2023 when Flexport acquired its technology.
rationale: Company shut down in 2023 and no longer operates, so there is no sponsorship case at all.
changed: Shut down in October 2023; technology acquired by Flexport
